vulnerability.name: Apache mod_userdir username enumeration
vulnerability.author: SecGen Pipeline
vulnerability.description: Apache's mod_userdir is enabled, so a request for /~username/ is mapped to that user's public_html directory. The server replies 403 Forbidden when the user's public_html exists (directory listing is off and there is no index) and 404 Not Found when it does not, so the response code leaks which usernames are valid on the host. This module creates the accounts and their public_html directories itself (override the usernames input to align with other account-creating modules in a scenario). CVE-2001-1013.
vulnerability.hint: The web server tells you which usernames exist
vulnerability.solution: Disable mod_userdir, or restrict it with "UserDir disabled" so per-user directories are not served
